why: Independent filesystem and Git fixtures protect fragment validity, newly added note requirements, existing-note ownership, CLI failure propagation and byte-preserving release rendering. The self-test never validates the mutation mirror's symlinked changes directory.

mutations.name: unknown categories pass validation
mutations.breaks: An unknown heading can be accepted as a pending release note.
mutations.find: if current not in CATEGORIES or current in sections:

mutations.name: product changes become exempt
mutations.breaks: CI, tooling and production changes can land without their own new note.

mutations.name: old pending notes satisfy the requirement
mutations.breaks: An existing pending note substitutes for the current PR's newly added fragment.

mutations.name: existing fragments can be stolen
mutations.breaks: A product PR can modify, delete or rename another pending PR's note.
mutations.find: if path.startswith("changes/") and path != "changes/README.md" and status != b"A":

mutations.name: the CLI ignores the comparison verdict
mutations.breaks: The command reports success even when its explicit Git diff requires a new fragment.

mutations.name: rendering drops historical bytes under optimized Python
mutations.breaks: Release preparation loses the original changelog history; tests must still detect this with assertions optimized out.
